At every blocklength $n\ge1$ its input and output alphabets are $\mathcal X^n,\mathcal Y^n$. For a block word $a^n\in\mathcal A^n$, regarded as a function on $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, use the one-based coordinate labels $a_i:=a^n(i-1)$ for $1\le i\le n$. With these labels, its block kernel is
$$W^n(y^n\mid x^n):=\prod_{i=1}^n W(y_i\mid x_i).$$
Thus the same single-use transition law is applied independently at each coordinate, conditional on the input word. This page imposes no feedback or input-cost constraint.
